Hvidovre Gastroenheden is a gastroenterology department participating in the Danish national quality program for inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), as evaluated in the DANIBD 2024 report [^src1]. The facility is notable for demonstrating a significant disparity in clinical practice compliance between two distinct quality indicators measured within the same department [^src1]. 

For Indikator 4, which assesses the administration of DEXA scans for patients undergoing steroid treatment, Hvidovre Gastroenheden recorded a compliance rate of only 20%, completing scans for 11 out of 55 eligible patients [^src1]. In sharp contrast, the department performed exceptionally well on Indikator 5, which measures fecal calprotectin testing for patients receiving biologic or immunosuppressive therapies. For this indicator, the facility achieved a 95% compliance rate, successfully testing 917 out of 965 patients [^src1]. 

This mixed performance is situated within the broader narrative of the DANIBD 2024 report, which highlights a general and severe lack of fulfillment of the 80% development targets for both indicators across Danish regions and departments [^src1]. Hvidovre Gastroenheden's data underscores the challenges and unevenness of standardizing monitoring and implementing evidence-based guidelines in IBD care, showing that high adherence to one clinical protocol does not necessarily translate to another within the same healthcare unit [^src1].
